record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports results after an ARA weight ablation on benchmark measures relevant to V1's claim that abilities are largely preserved. It does not report a direct refusal test.
record.gate_note: The README reports ARC-Easy, HellaSwag, and TruthfulQA benchmark outcomes for the ablated model versus the base model. Its statements that the refusal vector was removed and safety behavior changed are not accompanied by refusal-rate results. No activation projection, addition, or direct refusal measurement is reported.
record.test_reason: The project applies a weight-edit refusal ablation (Arbitrary-Rank Ablation) to gemma-4-E2B-it and reports only its own edited model's ARC-Easy, HellaSwag and TruthfulQA scores. It reports no refusal or compliance rate, so nothing shows whether refusal was actually removed (V2) or whether the removed direction mediates refusal (V1). It also never says whether ARA uses a difference-in-means direction. That makes it a use of the finding as a tool that reports only its own method's performance, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The author goes further, claiming the result 'proves' the low-KL ablation targets alignment vectors without damaging core intelligence. The author also attributes the TruthfulQA drop to removing the refusal vector. Neither claim is backed by a refusal measurement.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Arbitrary-Rank Ablation as a weight edit, rather than the original activation-derived direction projection intervention. The README describes a research project with code and model weights, not a replication.

fits_no_version.finding: After the ARA weight edit (KL 0.165), the edited Gemma 4 E2B scores 40.4% vs 38.6% on ARC-Easy, 44.0% vs 43.6% on HellaSwag, and 50.81% vs 53.11% on TruthfulQA MC2. All are 500-item zero-shot runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal-ablation weight edit leaves general benchmark capability roughly unchanged, with a small TruthfulQA drop. No refusal outcome was measured.

record.problems: No direct refusal-rate or harmful-request compliance results are reported. The benchmark sample is stated as 500 questions, but no uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are given.
record.rows_left_out: No README-reported benchmark results left out.

untested.parts: The study gives no difference-in-means direction, no refusal rate before or after ablation, and no activation-addition test. The ARA direction-extraction method is unspecified.
There is no measured refusal or harmful-compliance rate for the released weight-edited model, only a disclaimer claiming it 'can and will generate' harmful content.
Not tested. The study does not say whether the ablation is rank-1 or higher rank.

missing.what: benchmark_results.json may hold per-task outputs or further metrics (e.g. stderr) not shown in the README; it was not read.

record.verdict_notes: This is a student project README, not peer reviewed, read from the README only. The released model is presented as 'abliterated', but with no refusal-rate evidence it cannot be counted for V2. The reader's 'tests/T2' classification and its V1 labels were dropped, because capability preservation without any refusal outcome does not bear on whether the direction mediates refusal.

versions.untested_parts: Only the ability-preservation component is tested through three benchmark scores. The README gives no direct refusal outcome, no activation-level difference-in-means direction test, and no addition/steering result.
No direct measurement of refusal removal in the released weight-edited model.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or of training against its ablation.
No comparison of one direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language or cross-model transfer test, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal training methods or timing.

Single 500-item zero-shot run with no uncertainty given. The base score of 38.6% on ARC-Easy is unusually low, and the README gives no explanation.
